Abstract— This document gives formatting instructions for authors preparing papers for publication in the International Journal on Informatics Visualization.  The authors must follow the instructions given in the document for the papers to be published. You can use this document as both an instruction set and a template into which you can type your own text.  Please leave the space above the title empty. Space is intentionally spared for the journal title. JOIV requires the authors to cite at least 30 sources, and all the citations in-text must be synchronized with references. It is highly recommended to use a citation manager to ensure citation synchronization. The word number in abstract should be within 230-250 words and consists of objectives, materials, method, results, and implication for further research.
Keywords— Put your keywords here; keywords are separated by a semicolon.

Introduction

Authors are suggested to present their articles in the section structure: Introduction - The Materials and Method - Results and Discussion – Conclusion. The discussion should provide a bridge between results and the literature review in introduction. Please be sure that the citations are up to date. All the citations should be listed in the references. It is expected that the citations are at least 30 sources, and 70% are the publication within 2020-2025. The references should be in english. Use Mendeley for citation and references. JOIV requires authors to submit at least 6 pages article, excluding the references. Maximum number of authors is 6
Page Layout
An easy way to comply with the conference paper formatting requirements is to use this document as a camera-ready template.
Page Layout
Your paper must use a page size corresponding to A4 which is 210mm (8.27") wide and 297mm (11.69") long.  The margins must be set as follows:
Bottom = 28mm (1.1")
Left = Right = 14.32mm (0.56")
Your paper must be in two column formats with a space of 8.5mm (0.34") between columns.
Page Style
All paragraphs must be indented. All paragraphs must be justified, i.e., both left-justified and right-justified.
Text Font of Entire Document
The entire document should be Times New Roman at 10 points in size. Other font type and size may be used if needed for special purposes. Recommended font type and sizes are shown in Table 1.

Title and Author Details

Title must be Times New Roman at 18 points in size. Author name must be Times New Roman at 12 points in size. Author affiliation must be Times New Roman at 9 points in size and italic. Corresponding email address must be Times New Roman at 9 points in size. All title and author (s) affiliation must be in single-column format and must be centered.
Every word in a title must be capitalized except for short minor words such as “a”, “an”, “and”, “as”, “at”, “by”, “for”, “from”, “if”, “in”, “into”, “on”, “or”, “of”, “the”, “to”, “with”.
Author details must not show any professional title (e.g., Managing Director), any academic title (e.g., Dr.) or any membership of any professional organization.

To avoid confusion, the family name must be written as the last part of each author name (e.g., John A.K. Smith). Each affiliation must include, at the very least, the name of the company and the name of the country where the author is based (e.g., Causal Productions Pty Ltd, Australia).
Section Headings
No more than 3 levels of headings should be used.  All headings must be in 10pt font.  Every word in a heading must be capitalized except for short minor words as listed in Section III-B.

Level-1 Heading:  A level-1 heading must be in Small Caps, centered and numbered using uppercase Roman numerals.  For example, see heading “III. Page Style” of this document.  The two level-1 headings which must not be numbered are “Acknowledgment” and “References”.
Level-2 Heading:  A level-2 heading must be in Italic, left-justified and numbered using an uppercase alphabetic letter followed by a period.  For example, see heading “C. Section Headings” above.

Level-3 Heading:  A level-3 heading must be indented, in Italic and numbered with an Arabic numeral followed by a right parenthesis. The level-3 heading must end with a colon.  The body of the level-3 section immediately follows the level-3 heading in the same paragraph.  For example, this paragraph begins with a level-3 heading.

Figures and Tables

Figures and tables must be centered in the column.  Large figures and tables may span across both columns.  Any table or figure that takes up more than 1 column width must be positioned either at the top or at the bottom of the page.

Graphics may be full color.  All colors will be retained on the CDROM.  Graphics must not use stipple fill patterns because they may not be reproduced properly.  Please use only SOLID FILL colors which contrast well both on screen and on a black-and-white hardcopy, as shown in Fig. 1.

the colors used in each figure contrast well,
the image used in each figure is clear,
all text labels in each figure are legible.

orig_docx_paras: CLEAR3D-CT: Candidate-Based Lung Nodule Detection with Residual Learning and Attention

Abstract—Candidate generators in thoracic computed tomography (CT) produce many locations that are not reference nodules. We evaluate CLEAR3D-CT, a multi-scale volumetric classifier that reduces false positives among proposed candidates. A focal branch and two wider-context branches produce features integrated by cross-scale attention. An archived report describes a five-model ensemble with four reflection views evaluated on 89 internal LUNA16 scans using supplied candidate locations. Its competition performance metric (CPM), the average nodule sensitivity at seven false-positive rates, was 0.9043. At a prespecified candidate threshold, precision was 55.66% and recall was 85.51% on the natural proposal distribution. A separate 10-fold experiment using newly trained single models across 797 scans produced pooled CPM 0.6768; its training recipe and cohort differ from the ensemble evaluation. On 58 SPIE-AAPM LUNGx scans, an exploratory pipeline combining the frozen ensemble with a separate proposal generator achieved 47/70 target coverage and a fixed-distance CPM-like score of 0.4279. The latter uses incomplete target annotations and is not directly comparable to LUNA16. The results distinguish candidate ranking, nodule detection and effects of proposal prevalence while identifying the need for independent, matched evaluation.
Index Terms—computed tomography; pulmonary nodules; false-positive reduction; multi-scale learning; LUNA16; cross-validation
I. INTRODUCTION

Pulmonary nodule analysis in thoracic CT requires sensitivity to small structures while limiting the burden of spurious detections. Computer-aided detection systems often separate candidate generation from false-positive reduction: a first stage proposes locations, and a second assigns each location a nodule score. The Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) provides a widely used annotated CT collection [1], while the LUNA16 challenge defines both whole-scan detection and candidate-based evaluation [2].

Candidate classification does not recover nodules absent from the input proposals. In addition, a high accuracy on a heavily imbalanced candidate population can coexist with a low fraction of positive predictions that match a reference nodule. Reporting nodule-level sensitivity at stated false-positive rates alongside candidate precision and recall is therefore necessary to interpret performance.

CLEAR3D-CT is a candidate-based lung nodule detection approach using attention and residual learning within a two-stage 3-D CT framework. We study the supplied-candidate classification stage using a frozen ensemble on an internal subset, compare complete systems on repeatedly used development scans, and examine a distinct broader cross-validation recipe. We also summarize an exploratory external proposal-and-classification pipeline. These analyses do not isolate the causal effect of individual network components or validate attention as an explanation.
II. RELATED WORK
A. Multi-Scale Candidate Classification

Three-dimensional contextual networks learn appearance at different spatial scales [3]. Kim et al. used gradual multi-scale integration for candidate false-positive reduction and reported results for the LUNA16 V1 and V2 candidate sets [4]. Liu et al. reported a 0.912 CPM for a 3D asymmetric residual classifier [5]. Such results depend on the candidate pool, training split and inference procedure as well as the classifier.

Multi-scale designs address a practical ambiguity in nodule appearance. A small central field can preserve local texture, whereas a wider field places the same candidate in its surrounding anatomy. The study by Kim et al. reported different CPM values for the two LUNA16 candidate versions [4], illustrating why the candidate list and protocol must accompany a published score. Differences among published networks also include sampling, data splits and computational budgets.
B. Detection Pipelines and Evaluation

Recent two-stage systems combine a candidate detector with a reduction network. Li et al. reported 0.929 CPM on LUNA16 [6], and Wang et al. reported a six-fold mean CPM of 0.878 [7]. Zamanidoost et al. reported 0.9112 after false-positive reduction in a detector pipeline [8]. These whole-pipeline evaluations do not use the same input candidates or partitions as our 89-scan internal test. Table VI presents selected published results as context, not a paired ranking.

Evaluation based on the full CT volume places an additional requirement on the proposal stage: a missing proposal cannot be recovered by a classifier applied only to supplied coordinates. Reports that use a trained proposal network, an externally supplied candidate list, or fixed annotation-centered crops therefore address related but non-identical questions. The same numerical metric should not be interpreted as proof of equivalent input conditions.
III. METHODOLOGY
A. Task and Input Construction

For the main LUNA16 experiment, the input is a supplied candidates_V2 coordinate and a CT volume; the binary output is a nodule score. Prepared scans use 1 mm isotropic spacing and the recorded intensity window is −1000 to 400 Hounsfield units. The retained model source specifies a 33³ fine field, a 25³ context field sampled at approximately 2 mm spacing, and a 21³ central field taken from the fine input. A separate binding describes 27³ crops; the executed input path requires reconciliation before submission.

The archived input-construction code uses a validity mask when standardizing the fine patch. It constructs an intensity channel, a locally standardized channel and a candidate-centered Gaussian focus channel. The context channel uses statistics from the fine patch, allowing the two spatial fields to share a local normalization reference. These channels are an implementation of candidate-centered input construction; the Gaussian channel is not a radiologist-provided segmentation mask.
B. Multi-Scale Network

The network uses three scale-specific 3D squeeze-and-excitation residual branches. Each branch pools intermediate features into a 160-dimensional token. Scale embeddings and four-head self-attention combine the three tokens before a binary classification head (Fig. 1). The ensemble result describes the complete network and inference configuration; branch-level gains are not isolated by this comparison.

Within the archived model, convolutional residual blocks include group normalization and squeeze-and-excitation channel weighting. Features from different depths are pooled and projected to a common token dimension before cross-scale attention. Attention operates on the three scale tokens rather than on every voxel. The outputs are flattened and passed through a classification head. This description follows the retained model source and does not by itself demonstrate the independent value of any one branch.
Fig. 1. Schematic of the retained CLEAR3D-MSFv2 source and cross-scale attention. The focal field is cropped from the fine input; the executed crop binding remains to be verified.
C. Ensemble Scoring and Calibration

The preserved internal-test report identifies five fold checkpoints and four views (identity, X, YZ and XYZ reflections). It records a fit-side calibration scale of 1.70 and bias of 4.175479 and a natural-distribution threshold of 0.9999467. The training archive also contains eight-view out-of-fold scoring; that separate stage must not be conflated with the four-view internal report. The exact executed inference path and aggregation remain to be independently checked.

The archived internal report describes pre-sigmoid aggregation and fit-side calibration. The source archive includes different scoring paths, including averaging calibrated logits and averaging probabilities. The precise model-view aggregation used for each saved prediction set requires confirmation from the executed scoring script and checkpoints. The threshold is an experimental operating point, not a validated clinical decision threshold.
IV. EXPERIMENTAL SETUP
A. Cohorts and Data Separation

The manuscript records an active fit pool of 565 patients and 566 scans, 142 development scans and 89 internal-test scans. The internal report describes 112 reference nodules and 79,135 candidate rows, including 138 positive candidate labels. These counts describe different units. The test has been exposed through analysis; a related ledger also calls 83 component patients restricted and untouched. The scope and authorization of the recorded scoring require reconciliation.

The 138 positive test candidate rows should not be described as 138 separate patients or physical lesions. The stored CAD analysis uses 112 reference nodules for this subset, with duplicate candidate detections handled by the nodule evaluator. The fit and development counts likewise describe project partitions; they should not be confused with the complete 888-scan LUNA16 challenge cohort.
TABLE I. COHORTS AND ANALYTIC ROLES
The broader CV cohort contains 796 patients; the LUNGx subset excludes two prior pilot scans. Overlap and earlier exposure are not fully resolved.
B. Broader Cross-Validation and External Evaluation

A separate patient-assigned 10-fold experiment pooled 682,787 out-of-fold predictions from 797 permitted scans. It trained one model per fold for 12 epochs, sampling 4,000 eligible negatives per fold. This differs from the original five-model ensemble and its training procedure. The per-fold scoring outputs are out-of-fold for this experiment, but the cohort had prior project exposure and the provenance of the positive crop cache requires further independent audit. These results do not constitute a fresh, untouched test of the original ensemble.

The separate cross-validation script specifies 125 steps per epoch, batches of 12 positive and 20 negative crops, weighted cross-entropy with 0.015 label smoothing, and AdamW with a cosine schedule. The relation between its reported four-view scoring, calibration and saved predictions requires verification. This experiment is not the five-model ensemble evaluation.

For the exploratory SPIE-AAPM LUNGx analysis [9], a multiscale Laplacian-of-Gaussian proposal generator retained up to 4,000 candidates per scan. The frozen ensemble scored these candidates. Two scans used for a prior technical pilot were separated from the 58-scan analysis. The recorded matching rule counted a proposal within 5 mm of a target center. LUNGx was designed for nodule classification rather than exhaustive detection; non-target marks need not be confirmed clinical false alarms. Dataset overlap and the complete history of exposure remain unresolved.

The cap was selected using a development analysis, and the two pilot scans were separated in the archived report. The 58-scan analysis is nevertheless considered exploratory: the public challenge spreadsheet had been parsed before scoring, prior case overlap with the training corpus is not resolved, and the challenge annotations do not enumerate all findings that could be marked by a detector. A fixed 5 mm center rule is not the diameter-dependent LUNA16 matching rule.
C. Metrics and Comparisons

LUNA16 CPM is the mean nodule sensitivity at 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 false positives per scan [2]. We distinguish this nodule-level metric from candidate precision, candidate recall and F1. At a fixed threshold, precision is TP/(TP+FP) and recall is TP/(TP+FN), where counts refer to candidate labels. Raw candidate metrics retain challenge-excluded findings as labeled; LUNA16 nodule evaluation handles excluded findings differently.

For the balanced analysis, all positive internal-test candidate rows were retained and equal numbers of negative rows were sampled in 1,000 draws. This post-hoc reweighting illustrates prevalence effects; it is neither a new test set nor a patient-level confidence interval. The internal-test CPM point estimate is reproduced by interpolating the archived FROC curve. A valid confidence interval for the mean CPM remains to be recomputed from patient-level bootstrap replicates.

Each 1:1 resample retained the same 138 positive candidate rows and drew 138 of 78,997 negative rows without replacement, with 1,000 draws from a seeded random generator. This design changes the evaluated class ratio, not the model predictions. Variation across draws reflects the selected negatives; it does not incorporate uncertainty from the fixed positive patients, retraining or study selection. The 0.5 threshold used for this analysis differs from the prespecified natural-distribution threshold.
V. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
A. Internal Test Performance

The frozen five-model ensemble achieved internal-test CPM 0.9043 (Fig. 2 and Table II). Sensitivity was 0.7768 at 0.125, 0.9286 at 1 and 0.9911 at 8 FP/scan. The candidate-level results vary with the fixed threshold and the candidate distribution. At 0.9999467, the confusion counts were 118 TP, 94 FP and 20 FN, with precision 55.66% and recall 85.51%. At 0.5, candidate recall increased to 98.55%, while precision decreased to 13.09% (Table III).

Fig. 2. Archived FROC curves for the frozen ensemble on development and internal test scans. The development set was reused, and the internal set has known exposure; curves were not independently recomputed.

The raw internal-test candidate precision-recall curve has average precision 0.8429 (Fig. 3). This is an area summary for 79,135 candidate rows, not the nodule-level CPM. The two marked operating thresholds show the observed trade-off on this candidate distribution; neither marker represents a newly optimized test threshold.

B. Development System Comparison

Three systems scored 122,689 development candidates. The corrected audit reports CPMs of 0.9129, 0.8006 and 0.0975 for the Run 004 ensemble, CLEAR3D-HighRes and an in-house MedicalNet ResNet-18, respectively (Table IV). An earlier report gave MedicalNet 0.0030; a later inference log records replacing scores produced with mismatched raw crops and reports agreement with 1,060 saved scores within 1e−5. This supports, but does not independently establish, the corrected result. The systems had different training and inference budgets; this is not an architectural superiority test.

The comparator table permits inspection of the tested systems on identical development coordinates and labels. It does not equate the training populations, crop representations, optimizer schedules, checkpoint selection, ensemble size or test-time augmentation. The MedicalNet result therefore describes this particular in-house fine-tuning experiment, not a universal performance level for MedicalNet. Development-set reuse also prevents treating the comparison as an independent confirmation.
TABLE IV. EXPLORATORY DEVELOPMENT SYSTEMS
Identical candidate coordinates, but unmatched training, preprocessing and inference budgets. Average precision is calculated on the raw candidate population.
C. Broader Cross-Validation

The broader CV prediction file contains 1,387 positive and 681,400 negative candidate rows. At threshold 0.5, it yielded 1,324 TP, 9,592 FP, 671,808 TN and 63 FN: candidate recall was 95.46%, precision 12.13%, positive F1 0.2152 and macro F1 0.6040. Candidate ROC-AUC was 0.9958 and average precision was 0.4449. Pooled CPM was 0.6768, while the reported arithmetic mean of fold CPMs was 0.7235. The measures differ because averaging per-fold scores is not equivalent to pooling all predictions.

Across the ten saved fold curves, the CPMs range from 0.5007 to 0.8991 (Fig. 4). The fold assignment is project-specific, so its fold numbers do not denote the official LUNA16 subset numbers. Each fold curve uses a different held-out collection and a separately trained model. The range is descriptive and is not a confidence interval for an ensemble or a controlled estimate of a single design change.

The pooled FROC uses an archived evaluator with a 100-mark-per-scan limit. A later audit package includes an evaluator script, but the positive crop cache and the complete original training environment remain unavailable for independent reconstruction. Patient separation of cached positive crops, initialization and evaluator execution still require audit. The CV result is not the frozen five-model ensemble or an independent confirmation of it.
Fig. 4. CPM interpolated from the ten archived project-specific fold curves. The arithmetic fold mean and the score from pooled out-of-fold predictions answer different aggregation questions.
TABLE V. PROJECT-ASSIGNED CROSS-VALIDATION FOLDS
D. Exploratory External Pipeline

On the 58 LUNGx scans not used in the two-scan pilot, 47 of 70 target centers had a retained proposal within 5 mm (67.14% coverage). Under the recorded nearest-proposal rule, the CPM-like average was 0.4279. At the frozen ensemble threshold, 39/70 target centers were detected, with 154 unmatched marks (2.66 per scan). These results evaluate the proposal generator and classifier together. Incomplete target annotation and unresolved cross-dataset overlap prevent interpreting the unmatched marks as verified clinical false positives or this cohort as fully independent external validation.

For these 58 scans the fixed 5 mm proposal coverage bounds target detection under the specified pipeline: without a retained proposal near a listed target, the second-stage classifier has no candidate to score at that location. The observed proposal coverage should not be generalized to other proposal generators or interpreted as the classifier’s intrinsic sensitivity. The 58-scan subset also contains a limited number of target nodules, making its results sensitive to case composition.
E. Contextual Comparison with Published Studies

Table VI includes recent examples using the seven-rate CPM, together with our two LUNA16 results. The published studies differ in candidate sources, number of folds and the stage evaluated. The 89-scan test and broader project-specific folds are not equivalent to full official challenge cross-validation. Numerical differences are descriptive and cannot establish comparative superiority.

Almahasneh et al. reported 0.874 CPM for their integrated AttentNet detector with augmentation [10]. Silva and Pedrini reported 0.863 for a multi-view detector, using bootstrap-mean sensitivities after selecting fusion weights on cross-validation results [11]. Chou et al. reported 0.7795 for an adjacent-slice detector using whole-volume inference over 888 scans [12]. These are whole-detection systems, not supplied-candidate-only classifiers.

Lin et al. reported 0.901 CPM for their LUNA16-trained modified 3D region proposal network [13]. Mittapalli and Thanikaiselvan reported 0.948 CPM for a multiscale false-positive reduction model [14]. These studies are included to show the range of published approaches rather than to assign a ranking: differences in case selection, proposal generation, inference and score aggregation prevent a paired comparison with our internal subset.
TABLE VI. PUBLISHED LUNA16 CPM CONTEXT
Reported metrics are from different experiments and are not a head-to-head comparison. Wang et al. report a six-fold mean; Silva and Pedrini report a bootstrap-mean CPM.
F. Scope and Limitations

The internal test was exposed through analysis and is not external clinical validation; the authorization and status of its 83-patient component require clarification. The CV models and ensemble differ in training and scoring, and CV reconstruction remains incomplete. Natural and balanced candidate metrics reflect different prevalence. The archived internal CPM interval averages pointwise sensitivity bounds and is not a verified CPM confidence interval.

Prior data exposure, unequal comparator budgets and unresolved preprocessing and inference bindings limit independence and causal attribution. The LUNGx analysis uses a different proposal generator and incomplete target labels. The evidence does not establish clinical benefit, malignancy diagnosis, validated explainability or superiority over published systems.

An independent evaluation of the entire pipeline would require a locked proposal generator, prespecified operating points, sufficiently complete target annotations and a cohort with documented separation from prior training and model selection. Reporting proposal coverage alongside classifier results would identify missed targets that no second-stage classifier can recover. Such work would test generalization of a complete system rather than extrapolate from performance on preselected candidate locations.
VI. CONCLUSION

CLEAR3D-CT integrates focal, fine and context CT features for supplied-candidate false-positive reduction. The frozen ensemble obtained a reported 0.9043 CPM on 89 internal LUNA16 scans. A separate 797-scan cross-validation recipe and an exploratory LUNGx proposal pipeline produced different outcomes under different conditions. Further work should verify cross-validation provenance and CPM uncertainty, strengthen matched baselines and evaluate a frozen pipeline on a suitably annotated independent cohort.

def compute_candidate_metrics(y_true, y_pred, threshold=0.5):
    ap = float(average_precision_score(y_true, y_pred))
    p, r, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, y_pred)
    pr_auc_trap = float(auc(r, p))
    roc_auc = float(roc_auc_score(y_true, y_pred))
    
    pred_bin = (y_pred >= threshold).astype(int)
    tp = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 1) & (y_true == 1)))
    tn = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 0) & (y_true == 0)))
    fp = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 1) & (y_true == 0)))
    fn = int(np.sum((pred_bin == 0) & (y_true == 1)))
    
    n = len(y_true)
    acc = float((tp + tn) / n)
    prec = float(tp / (tp + fp)) if (tp + fp) > 0 else 0.0
    rec = float(tp / (tp + fn)) if (tp + fn) > 0 else 0.0
    spec = float(tn / (tn + fp)) if (tn + fp) > 0 else 0.0
    f1_pos = float(2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec)) if (prec + rec) > 0 else 0.0
    f1_neg = float(2 * tn / (2 * tn + fp + fn)) if (2 * tn + fp + fn) > 0 else 0.0
    macro_f1 = float((f1_pos + f1_neg) / 2.0)
    fp_scan = float(fp / 142.0)
    
    return {
        'threshold': float(threshold),
        'ap': ap,
        'pr_auc': pr_auc_trap,
        'roc_auc': roc_auc,
        'TP': tp, 'TN': tn, 'FP': fp, 'FN': fn,
        'accuracy': acc,
        'precision': prec,
        'recall': rec,
        'specificity': spec,
        'f1_positive': f1_pos,
        'f1_negative': f1_neg,
        'macro_f1': macro_f1,
        'fp_per_scan': fp_scan
    }

def find_optimal_threshold(y_true, y_pred):
    best_th = 0.5
    best_f1 = -1.0
    best_res = None
    for th in np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 99):
        m = compute_candidate_metrics(y_true, y_pred, threshold=th)
        if m['f1_positive'] > best_f1:
            best_f1 = m['f1_positive']
            best_th = float(th)
            best_res = m
    return best_res

def compute_froc_curve(scan_data: list[dict], indices: list[int] | np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    total_nods = sum(scan_data[i]['total_nodules'] for i in indices)
    if total_nods == 0:
        return 0.0, np.zeros(len(GRID)), np.zeros(1), np.zeros(1)
        
    det_list = [scan_data[i]['detected_probs'] for i in indices if len(scan_data[i]['detected_probs']) > 0]
    fp_list = [scan_data[i]['fp_probs'] for i in indices if len(scan_data[i]['fp_probs']) > 0]
    
    det_probs = np.concatenate(det_list) if det_list else np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
    fp_probs = np.concatenate(fp_list) if fp_list else np.empty(0, dtype=np.float32)
    
    y_true = np.concatenate([np.ones(len(det_probs)), np.zeros(len(fp_probs))])
    y_score = np.concatenate([det_probs, fp_probs])
    
    fpr, tpr, thresholds = skl_metrics.roc_curve(y_true, y_score)
    fps = fpr * len(fp_probs) / float(len(indices))
    sens = tpr * len(det_probs) / float(total_nods)
    
    order = np.argsort(fps, kind='mergesort')
    fps_sorted = fps[order]
    sens_sorted = sens[order]
    sens_grid = np.interp(GRID, fps_sorted, sens_sorted)
    cpm = float(np.mean(sens_grid))
    return cpm, sens_grid, fps_sorted, sens_sorted

        order_disk = np.argsort(curves_disk[:, 0], kind='mergesort')
        sens_disk = np.interp(GRID, curves_disk[order_disk, 0], curves_disk[order_disk, 1])
        cpm_disk = float(np.mean(sens_disk))
        
        # Also run vectorized matcher
        scan_data, cad_stats = precompute_luna16_matches(path, annots_csv, annots_exc_csv, series_uids)
        cpm_vec, sens_vec, fps_sorted, sens_sorted = compute_froc_curve(scan_data, np.arange(N))
        
        # Check numerical equivalence
        cpm_diff = abs(cpm_disk - cpm_vec)
        sens_diff = np.max(np.abs(sens_disk - sens_vec))
        print(f"{name} Official LUNA16 Evaluator ({t_eval:.2f}s):")
        print(f"  Official Disk CPM: {cpm_disk:.6f} | Vectorized CPM: {cpm_vec:.6f} | Diff: {cpm_diff:.8e}")
        print(f"  Official Disk Sens: {[round(float(s), 4) for s in sens_disk]}")
        print(f"  Vectorized Sens:    {[round(float(s), 4) for s in sens_vec]} | Max Diff: {sens_diff:.8e}")
        assert cpm_diff < 1e-4 and sens_diff < 1e-4, f"Numerical equivalence check failed for {name}!"
        print("  NUMERICAL EQUIVALENCE VERIFIED!")
        
        point_results[name] = {
            'cpm': float(cpm_disk),
            'sensitivities': [float(s) for s in sens_disk],
            'cad_stats': cad_stats,
            'scan_data': scan_data
        }
        froc_curves[name] = (fps_sorted, sens_sorted)
        official_eval_results[name] = {
            'cpm': float(cpm_disk),
            'sensitivities': [float(s) for s in sens_disk],
            'output_dir': str(eval_out_dir),
            'cad_analysis_file': str(eval_out_dir / 'CADAnalysis.txt'),
            'froc_txt_file': str(froc_disk_path),
        }

    # 4. Patient-Clustered Bootstrap Resampling (B=1000)
    print("\n=== RUNNING PATIENT-CLUSTERED BOOTSTRAP (B=1000, seed=42) ===", flush=True)
    B = 1000
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    
    bootstrap_samples = [rng.integers(0, N, size=N) for _ in range(B)]
    
    model_boot_cpms = {name: [] for name, _, _ in models_config}
    model_boot_sens = {name: [] for name, _, _ in models_config}
    
    for b_idx, idxs in enumerate(bootstrap_samples):
        for name, _, _ in models_config:
            cpm_b, sens_b, _, _ = compute_froc_curve(point_results[name]['scan_data'], idxs)
            model_boot_cpms[name].append(cpm_b)
            model_boot_sens[name].append(sens_b)
            
    bootstrap_stats = {}
    for name, _, _ in models_config:
        pt_cpm = point_results[name]['cpm']
        cpms_arr = np.array(model_boot_cpms[name], dtype=np.float64)
        sens_arr = np.array(model_boot_sens[name], dtype=np.float64) # (B, 7)
        
        cpm_boot_mean = float(np.mean(cpms_arr))
        cpm_boot_se = float(np.std(cpms_arr, ddof=1))
        cpm_ci95 = [float(np.quantile(cpms_arr, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(cpms_arr, 0.975))]
        
        sens_stats = []
        for g_idx, fp_rate in enumerate(GRID):
            s_vec = sens_arr[:, g_idx]
            sens_stats.append({
                'fp_rate': float(fp_rate),
                'point': float(point_results[name]['sensitivities'][g_idx]),
                'bootstrap_mean': float(np.mean(s_vec)),
                'bootstrap_se': float(np.std(s_vec, ddof=1)),
                'ci95': [float(np.quantile(s_vec, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(s_vec, 0.975))]
            })
            
        bootstrap_stats[name] = {
            'cpm': {
                'point': pt_cpm,
                'bootstrap_mean': cpm_boot_mean,
                'bootstrap_se': cpm_boot_se,
                'ci95': cpm_ci95
            },
            'sensitivities_grid': sens_stats
        }

    # 5. Paired Comparisons (Point Diff from Point CPMs, Bootstrap Mean Separately)
    print("\n=== PAIRED COMPARISONS (Calculated from Point CPMs & Patient-Clustered Bootstrap) ===", flush=True)
    comparisons = [
        ('highres_vs_run004', 'CLEAR3D-HighRes', 'Run 004 Ensemble'),
        ('highres_vs_medicalnet', 'CLEAR3D-HighRes', 'MedicalNet ResNet-18'),
        ('run004_vs_medicalnet', 'Run 004 Ensemble', 'MedicalNet ResNet-18'),
    ]
    
    paired_results = {}
    for comp_key, name_a, name_b in comparisons:
        pt_a = point_results[name_a]['cpm']
        pt_b = point_results[name_b]['cpm']
        point_delta = float(pt_a - pt_b) # POINT DIFFERENCE DIRECTLY FROM POINT CPMS
        
        arr_a = np.array(model_boot_cpms[name_a], dtype=np.float64)
        arr_b = np.array(model_boot_cpms[name_b], dtype=np.float64)
        deltas = arr_a - arr_b
        
        boot_mean_delta = float(np.mean(deltas))
        boot_se = float(np.std(deltas, ddof=1))
        ci95 = [float(np.quantile(deltas, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(deltas, 0.975))]
        
        paired_results[comp_key] = {
            'comparison': f"{name_a} minus {name_b}",
            'point_delta': point_delta,
            'bootstrap_mean_delta': boot_mean_delta,
            'bootstrap_se': boot_se,
            'paired_patient_ci95': ci95
        }
        print(f"Comparison: {name_a} vs {name_b}")
        print(f"  Point Delta (from point CPMs): {point_delta:+.6f}")
        print(f"  Bootstrap Mean Delta:          {boot_mean_delta:+.6f}")
        print(f"  Bootstrap Standard Error:      {boot_se:.6f}")
        print(f"  Paired Patient-Level 95% CI:   [{ci95[0]:+.6f}, {ci95[1]:+.6f}]")

    # Save FROC and Bootstrap JSON Audit
    froc_audit_data = {
        'status': 'PASS',
        'scope': 'Tasks 3 official development 142-scan LUNA16 FROC & patient-clustered bootstrap comparison (Corrected MedicalNet)',
        'cohort': {
            'scans': N,
            'patients': N,
            'total_ground_truth_nodules': 192,
            'fp_grid': GRID.tolist(),
        },
        'point_results': {
            name: {
                'cpm': point_results[name]['cpm'],
                'sensitivities': point_results[name]['sensitivities'],
                'cad_stats': point_results[name]['cad_stats']
            } for name in point_results
        },
        'bootstrap_stats': bootstrap_stats,
        'paired_comparisons': paired_results,
        'official_luna16_evaluator': official_eval_results
    }
    
    froc_audit_file = EV_DIR / "froc_and_bootstrap_comparison_audit.json"
    froc_audit_file.write_text(json.dumps(froc_audit_data, indent=2))
    print(f"Saved {froc_audit_file}", flush=True)

    # 6. Generate Publication Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6.5))
    colors = {'Run 004 Ensemble': '#1f77b4', 'CLEAR3D-HighRes': '#2ca02c', 'MedicalNet ResNet-18': '#d62728'}
    styles = {'Run 004 Ensemble': '-', 'CLEAR3D-HighRes': '--', 'MedicalNet ResNet-18': '-.'}
    
    for name, _, _ in models_config:
        fps_s, sens_s = froc_curves[name]
        cpm = point_results[name]['cpm']
        plt.plot(fps_s, sens_s, styles[name], color=colors[name], lw=2.2, label=f"{name} (CPM = {cpm:.4f})")
        
    for fp_val in GRID:
        plt.axvline(x=fp_val, color='gray', linestyle=':', alpha=0.45)
        
    plt.xscale('log')
    plt.xlim(0.125, 8.0)
    plt.ylim(0.0, 1.02)
    plt.xlabel('Average False Positives per Scan (log scale)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    plt.ylabel('Nodule Detection Sensitivity', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    plt.title('LUNA16 Official Scan-Level FROC (142 Development Scans)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
    plt.xticks(GRID, [str(x) for x in GRID])
    plt.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', alpha=0.35)
    plt.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=11, framealpha=0.95)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plot_path = EV_DIR / "froc_three_models_comparison_audit.png"
    plt.savefig(plot_path, dpi=300)
    plt.close()
    print(f"Saved publication FROC figure to {plot_path}", flush=True)

    # 7. Create New Small Audit Verification Package
    print("\n=== CREATING NEW SMALL AUDIT VERIFICATION PACKAGE (WITHOUT CHECKPOINTS/IMAGES) ===", flush=True)
    zip_path = ROOT / "clear3d_full_development_comparison_audit_evidence_20261109.zip"
    
    # Copy inference log
    mednet_log_src = Path("/tmp/mednet_corrected.log")
    mednet_log_dst = EV_DIR / "mednet_corrected_inference.log"
    if mednet_log_src.exists():
        import shutil
        shutil.copy2(mednet_log_src, mednet_log_dst)

    files_to_pack = [
        EV_DIR / "full_dev_predictions_run004.csv",
        EV_DIR / "full_dev_predictions_highres.csv",
        EV_DIR / "full_dev_predictions_medicalnet.csv",
        EV_DIR / "full_dev_predictions_medicalnet_mismatched_raw32_backup.csv",
        EV_DIR / "metrics_summary_audit.json",
        EV_DIR / "froc_and_bootstrap_comparison_audit.json",
        EV_DIR / "froc_three_models_comparison_audit.png",
        mednet_log_dst,
        ROOT / "score_full_dev_cohort_20261109.py",
        ROOT / "train_medicalnet_resnet18_comparator.py",
        ROOT / "run_medicalnet_full_dev_corrected.py",
        ROOT / "evaluate_and_audit_all_three_models_20261109.py",
        ROOT / "selection-001.json",
        ROOT / "balanced-candidate-classification-20261106-001.json",
        MAPPING_FILE,
        SUIDS_FILE,
        ROOT / "runs/comparator-medicalnet-resnet18-20261109/dev_predictions_1060.csv",
        ROOT / "runs/comparator-medicalnet-resnet18-20261109/medicalnet_resnet18_evaluation_summary.json",
    ]
    
    # Also add the official evaluator output directories
    for code in ['run004', 'highres', 'medicalnet']:
        d = EV_DIR / f"official_luna16_eval_{code}"
        for f in d.glob("*"):
            if f.is_file():
                files_to_pack.append(f)
                
    manifest = {}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for f in files_to_pack:
            if not f.exists():
                print(f"Warning: {f} does not exist, skipping")
                continue
            arcname = str(f.relative_to(ROOT)) if f.is_relative_to(ROOT) else f.name
            zf.write(f, arcname=arcname)
            h = hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            manifest[arcname] = {
                'size_bytes': f.stat().st_size,
                'sha256': h
            }
            
    zip_size = zip_path.stat().st_size
    zip_sha = hashlib.sha256(zip_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    
    manifest_audit_file = EV_DIR / "SHA256SUMS_AUDIT.json"
    manifest_audit_file.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
    
    print(f"Small Audit Archive created: {zip_path}")
    print(f"Size: {zip_size:,} bytes ({zip_size / 1024**2:.2f} MB)")
    print(f"SHA-256: {zip_sha}")
    print("=== AUDIT AND EVALUATION COMPLETE ===", flush=True)
